### Source and searches

Read git history/blame for resolution and cleaning; PRs #22, #23, #25–28, #31–32, #39, #41, #52; repository issues #12, #16, #38; PR #23/#26 review comments; original design commit `ee030be`. These PRs had no review/discussion comments or linked closing issues. No edits.

### Direct evidence

- [Current design, lines 65–70](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/blob/main/docs/funder-resolution-design.md#L65-L70): false flag selects “a unique usable same-member root payer in the immediate linked parent.” Rationale: “`IsUltimatePayerDifferent` compares the child's ultimate payer with the payer in its linked parent.”
- [Original proposal, lines 58–60](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/blob/ee030beb4a709f96f2deaac28f8f0a744acd9bdd/docs/funder-resolution-design.md#L58-L60): eligibility is exactly the same member's immediate parent and root payer. “Do not select an arbitrary donor group, follow grandparents, parse `via` text, or propagate the child's top-level names to its nested payments.”
- [Original proposal, line 206](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/blob/ee030beb4a709f96f2deaac28f8f0a744acd9bdd/docs/funder-resolution-design.md#L206): “Accept one-hop parent support in exchange for a rule justified by retained source descriptions. Broader inheritance needs another design.”
- [Issue #16](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/issues/16), johnnylarner, October 3: capture must retain separate names “so that attribution rules can change without losing alternative source evidence”; preserve missing values as null “so that acquisition does not invent source information.”
- [PR #23](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/23), October 8: adds payment-level reporting attribution while retaining donor/payer/ultimate roles separately. Git blame assigns the current parent-selection implementation to its squash commit `a533a8a`.
- [PR #41](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/41), October 9: replaces Python Splink scoring with native Rust, explicitly preserving payment attribution. Current attribution is Rust, not Python.
- [PR #26](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/26) fixes loader validation for children whose structural parent is unused; explicitly leaves resolution policy unchanged.

### Supported mechanics / inference

[Current implementation](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/blob/main/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/attribution.rs#L75-L101) filters observations by the parent declaration ID, same member, `Payer` role, and root source pointer. It never searches siblings. No eligible candidate produces `ParentEvidenceUnavailable`; one unusable payer produces `ParentPayerUnavailable`.

Sibling inference therefore is outside the documented and implemented policy. This conclusion follows from the eligible-observation rule; I found no explicit sibling-specific author decision.

Given your verified parent `versions[].fields.PayerName` and matching current HTTP names, these two records follow intended direct-parent attribution. A child's own null raw name is expected to remain null; the separate attributed name comes from the parent's observation.

### Gaps / attribution caution

The original proposal contains agent/cross-judge synthesis language. Its rationale is explicit documentary evidence, but **not an original human ruling**. PRs and issue bodies are attributable to johnnylarner; no human discussion specifically approving or rejecting sibling inference was found. Parent/child IDs `14765`, `15494`, `10624`, `11542` did not appear in the examined rationale.
